correctness.rationale: For the real Banaś–Frączek norm N(a,b)=max(sqrt2|a|,sqrt(a²+b²)), the unit input set splits into flat and circular strata. Pure flat-flat and arc-arc inputs obey F>=q=1+r²; the explicit mixed-stratum witness has F<q below r_c=sqrt(2-sqrt3), so minima are mixed. The displayed U=(1-r*sqrt(1-r²+r⁴))/(1+r⁴) solves (1+r⁴)U²-2U+1-r²=0 and yields unit x=(1/sqrt2,(2U-1)/sqrt2), y=(-v,sqrt(1-v²)), with v=[1-(1+r²)U]/(sqrt2*r). Both transformed outputs lie on corner rays, attaining F_*=(1+r²)²[1+(1-r²)U²]/2. The two-variable inequality (1) is bounded by a linear combination of its two max branches with weights ell in (-1,0), mu>0, |ell|+mu<1; the resulting quadratic minimization completes squares, proves its unique lower certificate globally, and matches the witness. At r_c the value agrees with published exact saturation 3(1+r²)/4, and r=0 value is 1. Independently minimized over two unit-sphere angular parameters using SciPy global differential evolution at r=.02,.1,.22,.4,.51: discrepancies from claimed F_* under 1.1e-9, and inspected 2,000-sample verifier for witness/weights. These samples corroborate but the algebraic dual certificate supplies the all-r bound.
residual_risks: The lower certificate depends on checking the stated exact weight positivity algebra for all 0<r<r_c; identity and bounds examined symbolically in proof, with finite numerical corroboration. No other clipping parameters or nonquadratic exponents are claimed.
